interest: Shows how U.S. diplomats tracked and compared official Japanese statistical publications amid 1930s government austerity.
keywords: Résumé Statistique de l'Empire du Japon
Embassy of the United States, Tokyo
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.501, covering July 1930 through September 1936) consists of five diplomatic despatches from the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Secretary of State concerning the procurement and routine transmission of the official annual statistical compendium of Japan, the Résumé Statistique de l'Empire du Japon. Initial correspondence in 1930 details the impact of Japanese government austerity measures, which temporarily ended the complimentary distribution of official publications to foreign embassies and raised questions about whether the Embassy should purchase copies at Yen 3.80, though a complimentary volume was soon secured from the Japanese Foreign Office. Subsequent despatches from 1931, 1932, and 1936 document the regular delivery of the 45th, 46th, and 50th editions to Washington for analysis by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and the Office of the Economic Adviser, reflecting the Embassy's ongoing reliance on official Japanese statistical reporting during the interwar era.
